Workouts, supersets and body measurements. The workouts export from the Hevy website works too. Routines and progress photos are not in either file.

Import each file on its own.

Workouts and body tracker entries. Use the spreadsheet export, not Backup: a .fitnotes backup file cannot be imported, so routines, workout comments and times of day, which only the backup holds, do not come across.
In JEFIT, open Settings and choose Export Data.
Save the CSV file it gives you. It holds your whole account in one file.
Come back here, tap Choose file and pick it.
Workouts, routines (as templates), body stats and custom exercises. Program schedules do not come across: Titan has templates rather than programs.
In Fitbod, open the Log tab, then its settings menu, and choose Export Workout Data.
Save WorkoutExport.csv to your phone or a drive.
Come back here, tap Choose file and pick it.

Your workouts and their sets. The Android app has no export of its own: ask Fitbod’s support for your workout data and import the file they send. Recommendations and muscle recovery do not come across.
In StrongLifts, open Settings and choose Export Data.
Save the CSV file, or share it to yourself. If the export is behind the paywall, use Contact Support in the menu: StrongLifts emails you the same file.
Come back here, tap Choose file and pick it.
Your workouts and body weight, from both layouts StrongLifts has written. The program’s next weights do not come across: Titan suggests its own.
Write one row per set, with at least a workout_date and an exercise column. Add reps, weight, duration or distance as you have them.
Body measurements go in a file of their own, with a measurement_date column.
Save it as CSV, then tap Choose file and pick it.
Column names are not case-sensitive and can come in any order. Every column, the units and the date formats are described on GitHub, with two example files to start from.
While the import runs, saving sets has to wait for it, and a long history can take a few minutes. You can finish your workout first, or import now.

Your history is already saved and stays. Only the photos not stored yet are skipped; importing the same file again stores them.
